jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI's Vendor Security team helps internal teams work securely with external products, services, and partners. Our work spans software, infrastructure, hardware, professional and managed services, vendor-provided workforces, data, and research. We build the programs and products that help teams understand vendor risk and put effective safeguards in place, protecting our customers, employees, and the company. About the Role We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work. You will independently lead vendor-security engagements: understand the business need, investigate the actual data and access, recommend a practical path, and work with the responsible owners until the safeguards are verified. You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead. This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. You should be comfortable taking a position, explaining the tradeoff, and changing your mind when the evidence changes. Success means internal teams can use vendors securely, reuse work that still applies, and understand what needs to happen next. In this role, you will: - Own vendor security engagements from understanding the business need through scoping, assessment, decision, treatment, and reassessment when material facts change. Make assessment decisions independently and use judgment about when to involve peers, specialists, or leadership. Route formal exceptions and risk acceptance to the appropriate decision owners. - Understand vendor use cases, workflows, user journeys, data flows, identities, access, integrations, and supply-chain dependencies. Identify plausible attack paths and their consequences for OpenAI. - Assess relevant architectures, configurations, controls, logs, and operational practices. Test whether the evidence supports the security claims that matter to the engagement, and make gaps and uncertainty clear. - Develop practical treatments, including changes to the operating model, data exposure, access, architecture, vendor choice, controls, or containment. Drive implementation with the responsible owners and verify that the treatment works. - Build reusable security patterns with clear applicability, safeguards, evidence requirements, exceptions, and review triggers. - Work with Legal, Procurement, and vendors on security addenda. Evaluate proposed terms and deviations against the engagement, explain their security implications, and develop workable positions with the appropriate decision owners. Legal leads wording and negotiation. - Learn from internal customers, agree priorities with the Vendor Security lead, and define the requirements, roadmap, and success measures for the bounded programs, products, and services you own. - Use Codex or comparable AI-assisted tools to build, inspect, test, and maintain practical improvements to scoping, evidence checks, routing, decision reuse, or treatment tracking. Investigate failures and own the result through adoption, continued operation, and explicit handoff or retirement. - Lead delivery across Security and partner teams. jobs.description: Job Description The Role: As a Chassis Diagnostics & Analytics Sub-system Lead Engineer, you will play a key role in shaping how next-generation vehicles are monitored, diagnosed, and improved. This is an opportunity to lead high-impact work at the intersection of diagnostics, data, and vehicle innovation—defining the capabilities that help enable smarter, safer, and more reliable chassis systems across braking, steering, suspension, and vehicle dynamics. In this role, you will turn complex technical challenges into clear, actionable solutions by leading diagnostic specifications, shaping core data strategies, and strengthening on-board health monitoring capabilities. You’ll collaborate across a broad network of partners, influence both technical direction and execution, and help build trusted analytics foundations that support the future of software-defined vehicles. If you are energized by solving complex problems, leading with technical depth, and making a visible impact on the future of mobility, this is a unique opportunity to help drive GM’s vision of Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions, and Zero Congestion. *This role is open to hire at 1 of 2 levels. (L6 or L7) What You’ll Do: Lead the requirements documentation and coordination by developing Behavior Technical Specifications (BTS’s) for chassis diagnostics and analytics projects and translating these to project initiatives, capabilities, and features. Create and maintain requirements for serial data and service-level diagnostics (ex. RIDs/DIDs) using “On-board Diagnostic Principles” and communication services. Organize and approve requirements written by other group members. Maintain privacy impact assessments for the data that the group collects and uses. Manage the data element tracking and sourcing strategy for the chassis space, including establishing required data elements, documenting source databases and tables, and proposing proper collection cadences. Develop and manage supplier data-sharing contracts. Develop and manage requirements for the data collection initiatives, capabilities, and features throughout the group by working with our IT teams to Demonstrate exceptional communication skills while reporting out to leadership (on a regular cadence) the progress of diagnostics and analytics development. Lead failure mode effects analysis and test regime discussions with our diagnostics and analytics developers. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): (Required for Level 6) Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Data Governance, or Data Analytics. 3+ years of experience utilizing data analysis methods and success solving complex problems. 2+ years of experience of working with vehicle telematics data, on-board diagnostics, or serial data. Capable of converting ambiguous problem statements into concrete project requirements. Passion for data driven results and customer initiatives. What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Skills): (Preferred for Level 6) Master’s of Science degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Data Governance, or Data Analytics. Chassis sub-system understanding (i.e. braking, vehicle dynamics, steering, and/or suspension systems). Proficiency using relevant programming languages: Python, SQL, Scala, & R. jobs.description: Are you excited about building the marketing engine for a new business from the ground up? We are looking for a Marketing Manager to own and drive growth for the Ring Appstore. This is not a traditional marketing role — you will run the full marketing motion for a business that connects hardware, software, and third-party integrations, taking responsibility for strategy, execution, measurement, and iteration. You will own marketing for two distinct customer segments: third-party developers who build apps for Ring, and Ring customers who subscribe and use 3P apps. Your mission: accelerate Ring Appstore growth by driving awareness, acquisition, engagement, and retention across Ring customers and third-party app developers. Key job responsibilities - Own the end-to-end marketing strategy for Ring Appstore, defining targeting, channel mix, creative messaging, and A/B testing to drive awareness through conversion and retention. - Design, launch, and optimize multi-channel campaigns including email, in-app, push, paid media, and Ring ecosystem cross-promotion, while analyzing performance metrics to continuously improve results. - Develop go-to-market plans for new app launches and partner programs, collaborating with product, engineering, developer relations, and business development teams to align on priorities. - Build co-marketing playbooks that empower third-party developers to promote their apps, and regularly review data to identify growth opportunities and experiment with new marketing motions. - Contribute to cadenced reporting and business reviews, translating funnel data into actionable insights and recommendations for leadership. A day in the life You will run the marketing motion for a new and growing business. On a given day you might review campaign performance data before joining a cross-functional sync with product and developer relations partners, then shift to drafting messaging for an upcoming app launch. You will regularly meet with customers (Ring customers who use apps, and Developers who build apps) to understand their needs, work across internal teams to remove blockers, and experiment with new growth motions. This role gives you the chance to run a full-stack marketing program for an innovative business that connects hardware, software, and integrations. About the team Ring Appstore is a third-party application marketplace for Ring cameras and devices. It enables developers to build, certify, and distribute apps that extend Ring's capabilities, from professional monitoring services to smart lighting integrations and beyond. The business is in a growth stage with an expanding app catalog, accelerating user adoption, and a maturing developer pipeline. We are building Ring Appstore to become the hub where Ring customers discover value-added services and where developers find a thriving market for smart home innovation.
